Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Neural pathways inside, etheric pathways outside", "body": "Chance reads Michael's formula aloud: just as hypnosis can establish neural pathways in the brain, what we call magic can establish etheric pathways in the world. Michael describes neural pathways as entrained routes linking a thought to a behaviour, laid by experience, repetition and strong emotion and set off again by anything symbolically similar, recalling touching his face in the mirror whenever he rehearsed a line he did not believe. Applying as above so below, he maps rivers onto the body's veins and arteries and argues that what he calls the planet's oldest river, the Susquehanna, anchors the first expressions of computing, globalism and wired electricity."}, {"title": "Skill that spreads through the collective", "body": "Chance says he first sensed a link between personal patterns and a collective field at music festivals, watching the average level of hula hoopers rise each year as more people practised, and he points to climbers who now free climb in hours big walls that first took weeks. He pictures skills as tunnels others have already dug. Michael calls flow arts, festivals and climbing the most human things imaginable, set against war as the most unhuman, and argues for a split where 20 percent competition brings out our best. In his outro Chance adds Rupert Sheldrake's morphic fields and a rat maze experiment he remembers hearing about."}, {"title": "Inception as a map of the dream", "body": "Michael rewatched Inception and reads it as a model of an engineered reality: a machine hosts the shared dream, its maze is designed by a psychology student rather than a coder, lucid dreamers work the mark, and when the subconscious senses something is wrong a second dream waits behind the first. He links this to Gnostic ideas of an archonic false reality, to Truthstream Media's Minds of Men on the cybernetics movement, and to the internet as the ultimate machine. Chance adds his idea of controlled awakenings, citing the Protestant Reformation and the QAnon phenomenon as moments where people thought they woke up but were steered into a new worldview."}, {"title": "Michael's hundred year plan theory", "body": "Michael describes what he calls a hundred year plan that began with the first computer, arguing that anyone born since 1945 has been hooked on the culture and technology of their earliest years. He ties the present moment to Jupiter and Saturn moving into Aquarius with Pluto to follow, and says the pressure now is to get people to commit to an inverted, anti-human expression of the Age of Aquarius, which he calls Robosapien rather than human. Because force would incur karma, he argues this dream runs on loopholes, and Chance asks whether a mass inception is steering the manifesting power of millions of imaginations toward a chosen outcome."}, {"title": "Navigating the dream as a human", "body": "Michael's approach to navigating the dream starts with separating human nature from second nature, which he describes as a learned neural pathway, and then tracing anything made back to its origins to ask whether it is in harmony with being human. Computers are his main example: he values being able to talk with Chance across distance but argues the industry rests on a foundation of decay, from rare metal extraction to slave labour. He says the trivium's rational mind must come before the quadrivium's imagination, and that waking up means getting back into the body through dancing, yoga, climbing and flow arts."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Michael Wann is a synchromystic researcher who uncovers occult correlations and connections between cultural phenomenon and our individual experience. In this episode we look at the movie Inception and what it reveals about the digital dream-world that humanity has mistaken for reality, the relationship between human neural pathways and macro-cosmic patterns in the universal mind, and the harvesting of the mass-imagination for the manifestation of a totalitarian age.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Imagination as the tool for the subtle world", "body": "Michael Wann describes the human body as a toolkit graded from muscle and bone for heavy work down to breath for smoke, and argues that for the most abstract layer, the realm of invisible waves and germs, the matching human tool is the imagination. He suggests that picturing the field around the body may support self regulation, while stressing he is no doctor and offering no medical advice. Chance Garton frames imagination as a perceptual portal, holding that a lack of imagination is what convinces people the world can only be the way it is, and that imagination itself loosens the grip of restrictive systems."}, {"title": "AI, screens and the voice in our heads", "body": "Chance Garton floats a theory that the truest artificial intelligence lives in psychic space rather than cyberspace: a superego shaped by government and religion into an artificial voice people mistake for their own thinking. Michael Wann answers with a confession of feeling pulled toward sharing his work through screens while also feeling repelled by the technology itself. He says he holds a healthy respect for whatever AI really is, and points to programs such as Project Stargate and institutes like Monroe and Esalen as signs, in his view, of how deeply consciousness research and the computer industry may be intertwined."}, {"title": "Questions about 5G, frequency and fear", "body": "Chance Garton asks whether the 60 hertz refresh rate of screens and the 60 gigahertz band associated with 5G hold symbolic meaning, and mentions reports he had seen linking pandemic symptoms to wireless frequencies. Michael Wann discusses those claims as stories circulating at the time, while warning that fear of invisible signals is itself a powerful tool of psychological warfare. He urges recognition without panic, then turns the number 60 toward time, the 360 degree circle and the Babylonian roots of astrology, arguing that etheric pathways show themselves through synchronicity and, most strongly, through mathematical resonance."}, {"title": "Self regulation, breath and the human design", "body": "Michael Wann argues that one of the quiet assumptions of the modern dream is that humans cannot control their own bodies, and points to Wim Hof and Eastern practices as hints that people may be capable of far more self regulation than they are taught. Chance Garton adds that breath may be the deepest control switch, the simplest binary rhythm in the body, and recalls accounts of native peoples enduring winter cold. Michael speculates that if humans were truly self regulating, scarcity based systems built on work and money would struggle to hold together, a view he presents as his own reasoning."}, {"title": "Make your own oracle and play the game", "body": "The conversation begins and ends with divination as play. In the pre-show, Michael Wann describes pulling an I Ching card and an Enchanted Map card before every interview, and later shows homemade cards built from Jon Rappoport's imagination exercises. He cites Francis Bacon's line that it is God's joy to hide treasure and the King's joy to find it. Chance Garton connects this to a self made divination scene in Twin Peaks and to his father's intuitive treasure hunting, and Michael encourages listeners to turn their own meaningful collected objects into a personal system for reading reality."}]

fields.Quotes JSON: [{"text": "Just as hypnosis can establish neural pathways in the brain, what we call magic can establish etheric pathways in the world.", "author": "Michael Wann", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/b7e0ef5f-142f-46eb-a25f-b387285ea071/MICHAEL-WANN.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "The more people that were doing something and becoming skilled at it, the more quickly someone that was new to it could jump in and get to a high level at it.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "We talked about war, and that's the most unhuman thing you can imagine. That was a controlled awakening.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "You have to at least begin with the idea that everything which is physical hardware is part of the inverse dream, and if you can't come to that, you are still in the dream.", "author": "Michael Wann", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/b7e0ef5f-142f-46eb-a25f-b387285ea071/MICHAEL-WANN.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Money is a frigging dream.
